messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected (p99 > 2.5s) for streaming endpoints in us-west-2. Scope: streaming-routing, prefix-cache. Metric spike started at ~2026-03-15T10:00Z. Hitrate drop on prefix cache from ~92% -> 37%. Potential cause: recent prefix-hash rollout (commit 0a1b2c) -- flagged by rollout-watch. Auto-escalation -> incidents channel.

Ava (oncall): I'm here, looking. Can someone grab p95/p99 over last 30m?

Sam (engineer): grabbing metrics, one sec. p95 ~ 420ms (ok), p99 ~ 2.9s (spike). Streaming tail stalls correlate with cache misses and paging spikes. I see a surge in paging reads to cold K/V buckets.

Jun (sre): same. Logs show repeated prefix-miss paths and a bunch of retries:

```
2026-03-15T10:02:14Z stream-handler WARN prefixcache miss key=kb:abc123 namespace=usr-v2
2026-03-15T10:02:15Z kv-client INFO read page attempt=1 key=kb:abc123 shards=[s3,s4] latency=210ms
2026-03-15T10:02:15Z kv-client INFO read page attempt=2 key=kb:abc123 shards=[s3,s4] latency=980ms
```

Sam (engineer): Confirmed correlation with prefix-hash change. After rollout we see new key distribution; many keys landed on recently-rotated buckets that don't have warmed prefetchers. Cache warming job didn't keep up. Hitrate drop measured across many namespaces.

Ava (oncall): Customer impact? Any errors surfaced to customers or only latency?

Sam (engineer): Mostly latency and streaming stallbacks. A few long-tail requests hit retry budgets -> transient 502s for some long streaming sessions. Estimated affected traffic ~6-8% of production streaming sessions in us-west-2.

Marta (PMO): Notifying CS on standby. Please post a short customer impact blurb when we have stable numbers.

Ava (oncall): Mitigation plan proposal: 1) temporarily pause prefix-hash rollout (rollback to stable mapping) 2) trigger targeted cache flush+warm for hot namespaces 3) route new streaming requests to fallback routing pool with pre-warmed caches (10% traffic) 4) increase prefetch workers by 2x for 30m. Thoughts?

Sam (engineer): +1. Also recommend disabling namespace salting for the rollout window; it amplifies key scatter and is causing extra cold misses.

Jun (sre): I can run the warmup job and bump prefetchers. Preparing commands now.

Sam (engineer): Deploy-bot, can we rollback prefix-hash rollout?

deploy-bot: Received rollback request for rollout prefix-hash-v3 (id: rollout-0a1b2c). Initiating canary rollback to prefix-hash-v2 across us-west-2. ETA ~ 3m.

Ava (oncall): While rollback runs: Jun, run targeted flush/warm for top affected namespaces (top 50 by miss rate). Commands below. Use conservative rate so we don't thrasher backend.

Jun (sre): Running warmup. Commands I used: 

```bash
# targeted eviction + warm calls for namespace list
for ns in $(cat hot-namespaces.txt); do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://internal-admin.us-west-2/cache/evict?ns=$ns" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"; 
  sleep 0.1; 
  curl -s -X POST "https://internal-admin.us-west-2/cache/warm?ns=$ns&rate=10" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" &
done
```

Jun (sre): Also increased prefetchers on the pool: `kubectl scale deployment prefetcher --replicas=12 -n us-west-2`

Sam (engineer): Monitoring metrics: after rollback started, edge hitrate climbing slowly. p99 dropping from 2.9s -> 1.6s in latest 4m. Still above SLO target but improving.

Ava (oncall): Good. Any sign of client-side confusion / session drops?

Sam (engineer): One spike of 502s at 10:07Z (retry budget exhaustion) but then recovered. No large-scale error storm.

Marta (PMO): Draft customer note suggestion: "We observed elevated streaming latency in us-west-2 due to a caching configuration change; we've rolled back the change and are actively warming caches. Some users experienced degraded streaming latency; no data loss. We'll follow up with a root cause update." Want me to send?

Ava (oncall): Hold until p99 below 1.5s for two consecutive 5m windows.

Jun (sre): Post-rollback status: prefix-hash rollback completed across canary and majority of nodes; rollout-watch cleared. Hitrate now ~78% (was 37%). Paging reads decreased ~62%.

Sam (engineer): Adding follow-up actions for post-mortem: 
- Investigate rollout gating for cache warm-up (improve readiness probes)
- Add preflight to simulate key distribution and estimate warmup time before rollout
- Make rolling-change more conservative for namespaces with > X RPS
- Add alert for hitrate delta > 20% over 5m

Ava (oncall): Agree. I'll capture these in the incident ticket.

Marta (PMO): Please add an owner for customer comms.

Ava (oncall): I'll own customer comms for this incident. Will prepare a concise update once stable.

Sam (engineer): One more note: observed one edge server with unusually high eviction churn. Created follow-up ticket #INC-7642 to investigate eviction policy correctness and whether the prefix-hash mapping caused hot-evictions.

Jun (sre): Handing off to night oncall (Nora). Summary for handoff:
- Cause: prefix-hash rollout led to key redistribution -> cold cache misses -> paging spike -> p99 latency breach.
- Mitigation: rollback to prefix-hash-v2 completed, targeted warm + prefetchers scaled, temporary 10% traffic routing to fallback pool.
- Current: p99 ~1.3s, hitrate 84%, paging reads normalized.
- Next steps: monitor for two hours, run eviction-churn diagnostic at 01:00 UTC, validate warmers are kept up during future rollouts.

Nora (night oncall via DM): acknowledged, will pick up monitoring and escalate if any regression.

Ava (oncall): tagging final metrics snapshot and closing live mitigation. Posting brief to incidents timeline and creating postmortem ticket. :white_check_mark:

Marta (PMO): Thanks all, please attach the postmortem draft to the ticket when ready.

incident-bot: Incident auto-log created: INC-7591. Severity: Sev2. Linked resources: runbook/prefix-cache, rollout-0a1b2c, postmortem-draft.

Ava (oncall): End of thread for live mitigation.
